core_obligations: Setup (proof lines 463-469): take two countable DLOs, form their partial-ismorphism set I - nonempty via the empty map - and aim to verify the Forth and Back properties.

Forth construction (lines 471-486): enumerate p's graph increasingly; for a new point a, split into the three cut cases (below all, above all, between consecutive mates) and pick b in the corresponding cut of the second order - each case a displayed item; density and no-endpoints license the pick in the closing sentence; q = p union the new pair is verified as a partial isomorphism because relational truth depends only on order type of the tuple.
Back and conclusion (lines 487-490): the symmetric property in one word 'similar'; the cited theorem converts the game to an isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Extend over any new left point by locating its cut on the right.
difficulty_reason: The classical uniqueness-of-Q argument (statement 458-461, proof 463-491): the three cut cases each written with their extension definition, the density/no-endpoints licensing explicit; the mirrored Back half named 'similar' at the same depth as other accepted parallel-case delegations, with the abstract engine it needs already proved. H2: complete construction modulo one named symmetric case.
